word-search.name: Word search
word-search.blurb: Find the hidden words in a grid.

typing-game.name: Typing game
typing-game.blurb: Type falling words before they land.

word-search.q1: How do you play word search?
word-search.a1: Find every word from the list in the grid of letters. Words run in straight lines across, down or diagonally, and on the hard level backwards too. Drag from the first letter to the last, or tap the first letter and then the last.
word-search.a2: Easy hides words only left to right and top to bottom. Medium adds diagonals. Hard adds every backwards direction as well.
word-search.a3: Common, family-friendly words in the language of the page, in eight themes such as animals, food, nature and sports. In Chinese, Japanese and Korean the grid holds whole characters.
word-search.q4: Can I play the same puzzle again?
word-search.a4: Yes. Every puzzle has a number. Type it with the same theme, size and level to get the same grid, for example to race a friend.
word-search.a5: Yes, in this browser: the words you found, the hints and the time. Your best time for each size and level is kept too.

typing-game.a1: Press Start. Words fall from the top of the field; type a word in the box and press Enter or Space (or just finish typing it) to clear it. A word that reaches the bottom costs a life; after three the game ends.
typing-game.a2: Yes. Every five words cleared the words fall a little faster, up to a top speed. Choose easy, medium or hard to set the starting speed.
typing-game.q3: Can I type in Japanese, Chinese or Korean?
typing-game.a3: Yes. Use your input method as usual; the word is checked when you finish composing. Japanese words also accept their kana reading or romaji, and Chinese words accept pinyin without tones.
typing-game.q4: Do I need to type accents?
typing-game.a4: No. Spanish and Vietnamese words are accepted with or without accents and tone marks.
typing-game.a5: One point per character of each word you clear. At the end you see the words cleared, characters per minute and your accuracy. Your best score per level is kept in this browser.

chinese-checkers.q1: How do you play Chinese checkers?
chinese-checkers.a1: Each side starts with 10 marbles in one point of the star. Take turns moving one marble; the first to fill the opposite point with its marbles wins.
chinese-checkers.a2: A marble steps to a neighbouring empty hole, or jumps over one neighbouring marble of either colour into the empty hole straight beyond it. Jumps can be chained, and you may stop after any jump.
chinese-checkers.q3: What if my opponent leaves marbles in my target?
chinese-checkers.a3: You still win once the target point is full and at least one of the marbles in it is yours, so marbles left behind cannot block you.
chinese-checkers.a4: Two: against the computer at easy, medium or hard, or with a friend taking turns on one screen.
chinese-checkers.q5: Is this the same as Sternhalma or the diamond game?
chinese-checkers.a5: Yes. Chinese checkers is a version of the German game Sternhalma, and the Japanese diamond game is a close relative.

word-search.lead: Play word search in three steps.
word-search.s1b: Choose a theme, a size and a level. A first visit opens an easy animals puzzle.
word-search.s2b: Drag across a word from its first letter to its last, or tap both ends. Found words stay coloured.
word-search.s3b: Find every word in the list to finish. Use Hint to see where a word begins.

typing-game.lead: Play the typing game in three steps.
typing-game.s1b: Pick easy, medium or hard and press Start.
typing-game.s2b: Type the word you see and press Enter or Space before it reaches the bottom.
typing-game.s3b: Three missed words end the game. Check your score, speed and accuracy, then try again.

chinese-checkers.lead: Play Chinese checkers in three steps.
chinese-checkers.s1b: Play the computer at easy, medium or hard as pink or blue, or two players on one screen.
chinese-checkers.s2b: Tap a marble to see every hole it can reach, then tap one. Chains of jumps cross the board fast.
chinese-checkers.s3b: Fill the opposite point with your marbles to win; a marble of theirs that never left can stay there.
